connections.why: The riddle of powers of seven that Ahmes set down as problem 79 turns up again in the Liber Abaci, as seven old women on the road to Rome, each with seven mules carrying seven sacks.
The Liber Abaci, for all its name, taught Europe to reckon in written figures instead of on the counting boards and cloths the abacus frame describes; Italy's 'abacus' manuals never show a board.

Al-Khwarizmi's book on calculating with the Indian numerals survives in Latin and gave us the word algorithm; Fibonacci learned the same nine figures of the Indians and taught them to Europe's merchants.
